gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-10 at Northern Arizona Wind & Sun (solar-electric.com) the APsystems EZ1-LV costs $281.78 for 900 VA, about $0.31 per VA, while the Hoymiles HiFlow Pro LV 360 VA and 420 VA units both cost $157.51 (about $0.44 and $0.375 per VA), so a two-panel setup built from two HiFlow Pro 420s costs $315.02 for 840 VA, which is more money and less output than one EZ1-LV.
standout_why: I compared against three cited pages. Solar Waypoint (updated 2026-11-04) lists HiFlow Pro LV at $149 (360 VA) and $169 (391 VA), and EZ1-LV at $325 direct (sold out) or $275 at SanTan. balconysolarkits.us (verified 2026-10-02) lists HiFlow at $149 'reported' and EZ1 at $325. pluginsolarcheck.com/kits/certifications (2026-10-18) has EZ1 at $325 sold out and no HiFlow price. All three give prices for each unit on its own. None works out cost per VA, none prices a two-panel build from single-panel HiFlow units against one EZ1-LV, and none has today's in-stock price from one retailer that sells both, so the two can be compared fairly.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's pick of the EZ1-LV for a two-panel plug-in system on price as well as output: at the same retailer on the same day, one EZ1-LV ($281.78, 900 VA) costs $33.24 less than two HiFlow Pro 420s ($315.02, 840 VA). The HiFlow Pro LV only wins for one panel ($157.51). Three of ChatGPT's other options drop out for reasons a shopper can't work around. The Enphase IQ8M is a 240 V rooftop unit rated 325 VA continuous with no plug (Solaris-Shop). NEP's BDM-1200-LV is rated only 800 W, has no price, and its page makes no UL 3700 claim. The EcoFlow STREAM Microinverter is sold out or pre-order at $369 and was paired with a STREAM Ultra that EcoFlow pulled from its US store (balconysolarkits.us). Dealectric lists no plug-in microinverter. Its Sun Gold Power inverters are 48 V split-phase off-grid or hybrid units, so none of our products belongs in this answer.
